title: Fleet Scaling Orchestration: interactive dashboard, policy editor, and immutable change history
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Ship a new Fleet Scaling Orchestration surface in the Console that unifies per-fleet scaling controls, throughput guarantees (floor/min), policy preview sandbox, and an immutable change history with quick rollback. This ticket covers the product requirements, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan for the first shipped iteration (Manager panel + policy editor + timeline).

Motivation: Customers on Dedicated capacity need a single place to set throughput SLAs, tune autoscaling policies for mixed-latency workloads, and verify operator changes. Current controls are fragmented between the Fleet Settings page and infra-only APIs which increases misconfigurations and incident surface area.

Key user stories:
- As a Platform Engineer, I want to pin a fleet to a minimum throughput (tokens/sec) so critical customers maintain baseline latency during traffic dips.
- As an SRE, I want to preview a policy’s simulated behavior for typical traffic patterns (burst, diurnal, cold-start) before applying it.
- As an operator, I want a readable, immutable changelog for scaling ops with the ability to roll back a policy to a previous snapshot.

Scope in this ticket (MVP):
- Fleet Scaling dashboard: real-time throughput vs. provisioned floor and 24h/7d histograms.
- Autoscaling Policy Editor: JSON + guided form mode supporting target throughput, scale-in/scale-out windows, burst headroom, and min-floor. Includes a sandbox preview with simulated traces.
- Change History Timeline: Immutable audit entries for policy changes, operator, timestamp, diff view, and single-click rollback to last-stable.
- Integrations: Wire up to runtime metrics API, audit log store, and RBAC checks.

Out of scope (future): cross-fleet bulk edits, RBAC granular approvals, multi-region routing UI, and on-prem air-gapped upgrade flow.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard shows provisioned floor and actual throughput; percent deviation metric computed and visible
Policy Editor enforces schema and warns on conflicting min-floor vs autoscale bounds
Sandbox preview runs a 5-minute simulated trace and produces expected scale events in UI
Change history entries are immutable, show diff + operator name + link to PR/Runbook
Rollback restores prior policy and emits an audit entry; rollback requires two-step confirmation
E2E tests for happy path apply + rollback and unit tests for policy validation exist in repo
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Wrong min-floor can cause sustained overprovisioning. Mitigation: Add cost-estimate preview and require explicit acknowledgement for increases >20%
Risk: Sandbox simulation might not reflect real-world cold cache behavior. Mitigation: allow uploading a small representative trace and label simulations as 'approximate'
Risk: Rollback of policy during flapping traffic could oscillate. Mitigation: impose cooldown period after rollback and surface guidance in UI
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): 10% of orgs with active dedicated fleets; admin-only access; monitor token-per-second, SLA-miss rate, cost delta
Phase 2 (Gradual): 50% usage with telemetry gating and feature flag for policy-preview sandbox
Phase 3 (GA): Open to all orgs; enable cost-estimate by default
metrics: SLO: reduction in SLA-miss incidents for pinned fleets (target 30% reduction over 30d)
Product metric: percent of dedicated fleets with a configured min-floor (target 40% within 60d)
Operational metric: mean time to detect misconfiguration via audit logs (target < 2h)
Cost metric: average percent change to monthly bill for fleets that enabled min-floor (monitor)
qa_steps: Manual QA: create fleet, set min-floor, generate synthetic load, observe throughput floor enforcement
Automated E2E: gitlab/ci pipeline runs sandbox preview job against mock runtime API
Security QA: verify RBAC-enforced endpoints reject unauthorized modifications
Load QA: simulate 1k concurrent policy updates (to ensure timeline append performance)
